findings.subject: Vessel course tubes — idle opacity (branches out-shine the committed trunks)
findings.field: src/components/viewer3d/TractTube.tsx:339-352 (stepTractFrame), :322-329 (TractFrameEntry), :423-445 (material memo); src/components/viewer3d/NucleusMesh.tsx:48-56 (KIND_OPACITY.vessel = 0.5), :186-187
findings.claimed: v18 E2 gives a vessel course the ARTERIAL material — `createVesselMaterial(tract.color)`, opacity 0.5, depthWrite false — "the same material family the committed artery GLBs get" (PLAN.md §2.2)
findings.expected: once the frame lerp settles (≈0.3 s at 8/s), a vessel tube holds opacity 0.5 and depthWrite false, exactly like the artery it branches from (NucleusMesh pins opacity = KIND_OPACITY.vessel = 0.5 and depthWrite = false)
findings.basis: Measured by executing the shipped factory and reading the shipped frame pass: factory opacity 0.50 / depthWrite false, but `TractFrameEntry` carries no idle-opacity field and `stepTractFrame` lerps `material.opacity` toward 1 (`material.opacity = THREE.MathUtils.lerp(material.opacity, entry.dimmed ? 0.15 : 1, alpha)`) with `material.depthWrite = material.opacity > 0.99`. The committed artery in the same view stays at 0.5 / no depth write. Internal contradiction: the same defect is named as edit E6 in the v18 plan of record (PLAN.md §2.5, "the branches would read brighter and more solid than the arteries they branch from") and was never applied.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `idleOpacity: number` to `TractFrameEntry` (= 0.5 when `variant === "vessel"`, else 1), publish it in the registry effect, and lerp toward `entry.dimmed ? 0.15 : entry.idleOpacity` (v18 PLAN.md E6, one field + one line).
findings.notes: Exactly the 79 drawn vessel tubes are affected (41 courses + 38 mirrored twins, measured `registryVesselParts()`/vessel-render §2); a 0.5-opacity fresnel preset driven to 1.0 also loses the fresnel rim the factory adds (`applyFresnelOpacity` boost 1.5).

findings.subject: The gray-matter preset is unreachable — 12 parts declare it, none renders with it
findings.field: src/geometry/materials.ts:215-237 (createEnvelopeMaterial), :474-489 (makeAnatomyMaterial); src/geometry/generated.ts:17-27 ("materialHint — Preset for the central material factory"); src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:303-305 (ghost materials), :375-377 (envelope materials); src/assets/anatomy/anatomy-manifest.json
findings.claimed: The manifest schema documents `materialHint` as the preset each part renders with, and materials.ts documents the gray-matter envelope (roughness 0.62, opacity 0.42, #b7a8a4 base, fresnel rim) as a live family

findings.basis: Executed census over all 138 parts: 12 declare gray-matter (10 ENVELOPE_SLOTS + the 2 hemisphere shells), 0 of them reach `makeAnatomyMaterial("gray-matter")`. The envelope pass builds `createContextMaterial(CONTEXT_COLOR)` for all 10 slots (opacity mutated to 0.16 / 0.45 lit, #94a3b8) and the ghost pass builds `createGhostShellMaterial` (0.14, #9fb0c4). `createEnvelopeMaterial` has ZERO call sites in src/ (grep over SceneLayers, NucleusMesh, TractTube, SomatotopyOverlay, PlaneHelpers, SectionCanvas). findings.suggestedFix: Decide one truth and make the declaration match the render: either draw the 10 gray-matter slot parts with `createEnvelopeMaterial` (0.42, warm tissue) or re-hint those manifest rows to `context` (a manifest-hint edit, not a re-bake — the GLBs and their bboxes stay frozen). findings.notes: Pixel consequence if the 0.42 grey-matter preset were honoured: the pons, medulla, midbrain, thalamus, hypothalamus, cerebellum and pineal silhouettes (106k+ tris) would become 2.6× more opaque and warm instead of slate. Neither reading is a crash; the defect is that the declared hint is not the rendered preset and the documented factory is dead.

findings.subject: Cranial-nerve tubes render pale sage while their section contour, tree chip and legend use #14b8a6
findings.field: src/components/viewer3d/TractTube.tsx:429-431 (nerve courses take `createTractMaterial`); src/geometry/materials.ts:252-256 (base tinted 45 % toward the record colour); src/components/section/sectionAssets.ts:215-227 (`courseMeta` uses the taxonomy colour); src/data/taxonomy.json
findings.claimed: v18 E1: the twelve nerve tubes take the plain white-matter tract preset — PLAN.md §6 expects "12 nerve tubes pale/white-matter"
findings.expected: per the project's own cross-surface colour rule — stated for the vessel family in v18 PLAN.md §2.3 ("the 2D surface … is the reference the 3D surface should match") and measured 40/40 for courses — the nerve tube colour should agree with the 2D contour colour the same record paints

findings.subject: The parametric ventricle envelopes are loading stand-ins, not the rendered body (docstring says otherwise)
findings.field: src/geometry/envelope.ts:256-273 (ventricleGeometryFor); src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:399-408, :751; src/components/viewer3d/NucleusMesh.tsx:202 `shownGeometry = glbGeometry ?? geometry`

findings.subject: The caudate nucleus and the choroid plexus are drawn by no 3D pass at all (LINKS says render: "body" and the content-only set suppresses them)
findings.field: src/geometry/anatomyAssets.ts:194-232 (TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS contains nuc-caudate-head/-body/-tail and vent-choroid-plexus-lateral), :247-249 and :267 (`render: "body"` for nuc-caudate-head → ctx-caudate-l, and for vent-choroid-plexus-lateral → ctx-choroid-plexus-l); src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:180-187 (`isGhostOrContentOnly` is the only suppression)
findings.claimed: TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS header (anatomyAssets.ts:177-192): every record listed "is either a cortex record (whose body IS the ghost shell) or a redirection to a body that a neighbouring record already draws" — so suppressing it loses only a duplicate
findings.expected: every committed body reaches the screen through at least one admitted record
findings.basis: Executed over all 138 manifest parts and the shipped visibility predicates: 11 parts are drawn by no 3D pass. Nine are `-r` twins the mirror rule replaces (see mir-3) — but TWO are bodies no record draws on either side: ctx-caudate-l (3,152 tris) + ctx-caudate-r (3,212 tris) and ctx-choroid-plexus-l (1,520) + ctx-choroid-plexus-r (1,512). Their only owners (nuc-caudate-head/-body/-tail, vent-choroid-plexus-lateral) are in TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS, and no other record claims those slugs, so the premise "a neighbouring record already draws it" is measurably false for both families: the caudate nucleus and the choroid plexus are invisible in the 3D viewer while the 2D section (which loads all 138 GLBs) paints them.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each family one drawing record: either drop those ids from TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS and let the LINKS owner draw (nuc-caudate-head, vent-choroid-plexus-lateral already carry `render: "body"`), or point a neighbour at the body — and if a family should draw both sides, name `bodyRight`, because ctx-caudate-r and ctx-choroid-plexus-r are referenced by NO record at all, so only the mirror rule can ever put them on screen. Verify with the same census (138 parts, 0 with no pass); a gate assertion could pin it.
findings.notes: Visible consequence: the dorsal striatum is one of the atlas's basal-ganglia subjects and the user cannot see it in 3D; the choroid plexus is likewise absent. Both remain selectable and both appear in the live section, so the defect is 3D-only.

findings.subject: Two committed bodies are drawn TWICE at identical coordinates, and `render: "none"` is read by no renderer
findings.field: src/geometry/anatomyAssets.ts:121-138 (AnatomyRender documents `none` = "deliberately NOT drawn"), :240 and :253 (`render: "none"` for tract-corpus-callosum-body, `render: "body"` for ctx-lenticular-nucleus — both pointing at a body another record also draws), :404-407 (`isGhostOrContentOnly` reads only `render === "ghost"`); src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:688-793
findings.claimed: The `render` flag is the schema's way of saying how (or whether) a record reaches the 3D scene; `none` means the body belongs to a neighbour
findings.expected: each committed body is drawn once per side, and a `render: "none"` link never mounts a second mesh
findings.basis: Executed census of admitted records per body slot. Default framing (the shipped store's own boot layers, 32 ids hidden): ctx-putamen-l and its right twin are each drawn TWICE — nuc-putamen (kind nucleus, #d97706, opaque, 2,340 tris) and ctx-lenticular-nucleus (kind context, #94a3b8, opacity 0.22) mount the same GLB at the same transform. All layers on, nothing hidden: ctx-corpus-callosum (+ its right twin) is likewise drawn twice by ctx-corpus-callosum and tract-corpus-callosum-body (16,512 tris each). Grep over SceneLayers/NucleusMesh/sectionAssets/anatomyAssets finds exactly ONE read of the link's `render` flag in the whole app (`isGhostOrContentOnly`, `render === "ghost"`); `none` is honoured nowhere, so the only de-duplication is the hand-maintained TEL_CONTENT_ONLY_IDS list — which misses both of these ids.
findings.suggestedFix: Either read `render === "none"` in the structure pass (one predicate beside the existing `ENVELOPE_RECORD_IDS`/somatotopy/course suppressions, which is the same shape), or add `tract-corpus-callosum-body` and `ctx-lenticular-nucleus` to the content-only set. Reading the flag is preferable: it makes the schema's own word authoritative instead of a parallel list.
findings.notes: Certain from the census: two meshes per body with identical geometry and transform, one opaque and one translucent. Inferred and stated as such: coplanar surfaces at the same depth are the classic z-fighting/over-blend condition in a depth-tested rasteriser (three.js docs, "Transparency" / depth-sorting notes); the exact pixel artefact needs a live page, which this sandbox cannot run.

findings.subject: Eight of the 23 tracts are mirrored although their authored chain already crosses the midline (doubled crossings)
findings.field: src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:794-808 (`const paired = getTaxonomyEntry(tract.id)?.laterality === "paired"`), comment at :800-802; src/data/taxonomy.json laterality for the 23 tracts.json ids; src/data/tracts.json waypoints
findings.claimed: SceneLayers.tsx:800-802: "Tracts registered `midline` (the decussations, the commissures) stay single — mirroring those would duplicate the crossing itself"
findings.expected: a tract whose authored chain crosses x = 0 is drawn once (or the guard is stated as not applicable)
findings.basis: Measured: ALL 23 tracts are registered `paired` (23/23; 0 midline), so the documented guard fires for no tract at all. Eight of the 23 have waypoint ranges that span both sides of x = 0 and are therefore drawn twice: tract-corticospinal-lateral x −3.0…6.5 · tract-corticopontine −6.5…6.0 · tract-rubrospinal −3.5…3.0 · tract-tectospinal −1.5…2.0 · tract-dcml −6.0…2.0 · tract-trigeminothalamic-ventral −3.8…5.5 · tract-anterior-spinocerebellar −5.0…6.5 · tract-auditory-pathway −4.5…6.5. Each is a decussating pathway by name (pyramidal/ventral tegmental/dorsal tegmental decussations, the internal arcuate fibres of the medial lemniscus, the anterior spinocerebellar double crossing, the crossed trigeminothalamic and auditory projections — Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, ch. 5-6, 11; Patten, Neurological Differential Diagnosis), i.e. the authored chain is already bilateral and the mirror adds a second, coincident tube over the crossing segment (double opacity, coplanar surfaces → z-fighting at the crossing).
findings.suggestedFix: Either register the crossing tracts `midline` in taxonomy.json (one field per record, the guard then does what its comment says) or add the code test the comment implies before mounting the twin: skip the mirror when the authored chain spans both signs of x (`Math.min(...xs) < 0 && Math.max(...xs) > 0`). Record which tracts stay single in the same change.
findings.notes: The tract laterality is what `isTractVisible` and the mirror decision both read, so the fix is data-only for the registry route. The v17 mirror work is otherwise correct: the twin selects/hovers/labels as the same record (see mir-4).

findings.subject: A registry-midline artery (SCA vermian branches) is drawn once, 1.2–6.4 mm off the midline
findings.field: src/geometry/vasculature-courses.ts — vasc-sca-vermian-branches (laterality midline, waypoints x 1.0…5.3); src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx:836 (`isPairedVessel`) → single tube
findings.claimed: The course is registered `midline`; SceneLayers.tsx:833-834: "a midline one (the anterior spinal artery, the vermian branches) stays single — mirroring a midline vessel would double it"
findings.expected: a midline vessel's authored chain runs on the midline (|x| ≈ 0), so the single tube is the midline structure
findings.basis: Measured over all 41 vessel courses: 3 are midline and drawn single. Two are genuinely centred — vasc-pontine-perforating-arteries mean x = 0.68 au (range −0.0…1.8) and vasc-anterior-spinal-artery mean x = 0.17 au (−0.1…0.8). The third, vasc-sca-vermian-branches, has mean x = 3.81 au and range 1.0…5.3 au = 1.2…6.4 mm lateral, i.e. the atlas shows the superior cerebellar artery's vermian branches as one tube wholly on the patient-left side, while the vermis they supply is the midline structure between the hemispheres (Blumenfeld ch. 5; Snell, Clinical Neuroanatomy, cerebellum).
findings.suggestedFix: Either re-author the course onto the midline (mean |x| < 1 au, matching the other two midline vessels) or, if the intent is "the vermian branches of one side", register the course `paired` so both sides draw.
findings.notes: Severity is minor because the object is one thin tube among 79 in the vasculature view; the class (a midline-labelled structure drawn one-sided) is what matters.

findings.subject: Live-section hit test picks a CONTAINER, not the smallest structure under the cursor (the known precedence defect is still present)
findings.field: src/components/section/SectionCanvas.tsx:1219-1243 (`visible` sorted by `kindRankOf(meta.kind)` only; `visibleFaces = [...items].reverse()`), :2192-2233 (`hitTest` returns the first face whose loops contain the point), docstring at :2180-2191

findings.basis: Measured by reproducing the shipped rule over the shipped geometry (all 138 committed GLBs + 103 procedural course parts sliced with the shipped `extractContours`, tested with the shipped `pointInLoops`): the contested sample points are the vertices of one part that lie inside another. Axial planes y = −24…48: 1,392 contested points, 738 lie inside ≥2 contours, 122 (16.5 %) select a LARGER container. Coronal z = −24…48: 1,122 inside ≥2, 201 failures (17.9 %). Sagittal x = −24…48: 662 inside ≥2, 63 failures (9.5 %). Total 2,522 evaluated points, 386 failures (15.3 %); in 0 of them does the click land on a part that does not contain the point, so the defect is purely "which container wins". Same-kind failures dominate (89/122 axial, 164/201 coronal, 58/63 sagittal) because within one kind the winner is simply the manifest-later part. Named examples (winner/smallest contour area): nuc-inferior-olive-medial ← nuc-medullary-reticular ×24.7 · nuc-paraventricular ← nuc-thalamic-anterior ×19.6 · nuc-subthalamic ← nuc-vl ×15.3 · nuc-dorsal-raphe ← nuc-oculomotor ×13.3 (axial y = 14) · ctx-hypothalamus-surface ← ctx-thalamus-r ×7.1 at 17 points (z = 0/6) · ctx-cerebellar-vermis ← ctx-cerebellum-r ×5.0 at 14 points (y = −24/−8/0) · nuc-lgn ← tract-optic-tract-l ×2.9 at 19 points (y = 14) · nuc-arcuate-hypothalamic ← nuc-ventromedial ×1.5 at 13 points (z = 6).
findings.suggestedFix: Make containment, not kind rank, the tie-breaker: order `visibleFaces` by drawn area (smallest first) within the existing kind buckets — one comparator, no new state — or sort the hit list by `drawnArea` at `ensureRenderOrder` time. findings.notes: The docstring is the contract the code violates; the fix is small and local. Note the label pass already computes per-loop areas (`polygonAreaOf`), so an area-ordered hit list costs one extra sort on the cache rebuild, not per pointermove.

findings.suggestedFix: Swap the two badges (A → x=748, P → x=52) — the artwork already matches the app convention, so the fix is two text/circle pairs in the SVG, not a re-draw.
findings.notes: Highest-value plates finding: an inverted A/P label on a hemisphere plate mislocates every structure the reader identifies from it.
